name: Arno Blue
lede: Arno Blue is a muted, greenish slate blue recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1928, its name recalling the river that runs through Florence and Pisa.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates this blue to 1928, plate 37, swatch J 6 [1]. The name's link to Italy's Arno River is a reasonable reading, given the hue, but the dictionary entry does not state it, so it stays undocumented here [1]. The nearest color-graph neighbor is [[teal-blue]], 4.1 units away, with [[dark-orient-blue]] close behind at 4.2, and [[venezia]] and [[delft-blue]] close by [2].

Munsell gives 6.7B 4.5/3.5, a low-saturation, medium-dark blue-green [1]. The hex #4B7180 is a screen approximation of the dictionary plate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 159 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.67 percent, as photographed [3]. It is strongest in work by Jean-Léon Gérôme (nearly 25 times the archive's base rate) and Claude Monet (almost 18 times), including Monet's *Low Tide at Pourville, near Dieppe* (1882) and Gérôme's *Head of an Italian Woman* (1847) [3]. James McNeill Whistler's *Violet and Silver—The Deep Sea* (1893) and Giovanni Battista Tiepolo's *Saint Roch Carried to Heaven by Angels* (1735) also carry it strongly [3]. The 1720s show the sharpest decade-level concentration, about four times average [3]. These are computed matches on photographed, varnished canvases [3].
